unit.why: A homily from the Hida (Devash Lefi) on 'whoever forgoes his due' that embeds a short anecdote about R. Hayyim ben Attar and a scholar who forgave a rich man at once; the anecdote is a narrated event but sits inside a homiletic frame.

stories.start_quote: כי היה עובדא דעשיר אחד תקיף
stories.end_quote: וזהו מדה כנגד מדה ודו״ק היטב
stories.summary_en: A powerful rich man insulted a Torah scholar. R. Hayyim ben Attar urged the scholar to forgive him, and the scholar said he had already forgiven at once, so that the rich man's sin would not burden the Shekhinah. The rabbi was pleased, and the author draws from this a rationale for why one who forgoes his due is forgiven his sins.

tags.why: the anecdote is wrapped in an exegetical frame explaining a talmudic dictum
